audit.whatIsWrong: The page gives Yone five of seven rows and the prose says Maokai has "almost no kill pressure" — against a 47.42% win rate over 1280 games. The packet itself carries the defect note: "level chart contradicts data".
audit.why: The mirror audit set the chart to Yone / Maokai / Maokai / Skill / Skill / Skill / Yone, which fits both the win rate and Maokai's actual laning: Twisted Advance is a 14s untargetable dash-root, Bramble Smash knocks back every 7s, and Sap Magic heals the chip back.
audit.corrected: Row 0 to Yone, rows 1 and 2 to Maokai, row 5 to Skill on BOTH layers as one group, with the phase whys and whys[1], whys[2], whys[5] rewritten to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[0].text contains a literal corruption — "his Sapling Toss (W... E) poke" — and Bramble Smash is never mentioned anywhere on the page. Twisted Advance is described only as a "lock-on root".
audit.why: Twisted Advance makes him UNTARGETABLE while he dashes, then roots on arrival — burst spent into that dash is burst wasted, which is the single most useful thing to know here. Bramble Smash is a 7s knockback that interrupts your Q3 dash, and Sapling Toss is 18s at rank 1 from 1100 range.
audit.corrected: Named all three with cooldowns across spikes[0].text, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t, dosFull[0].d, early and mid, and fixed the corrupted slot label.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldowns anywhere, and breakdown.late describes Fate Sealed as setting up "team knockups nothing can dodge".
audit.why: Fate Sealed is a pull, not a knockup. Nature's Grasp is 130s at rank 1 and Twisted Advance 14s — the 14s is the window the whole lane is played around, and it needed to be on the page.
audit.corrected: Wrote 14s / 7s / 130s into the relevant fields and corrected Fate Sealed to a pull in breakdown.late.

audit.whatIsWrong: report[8].t recommends Executioner's Calling but no field says when his healing actually happens.
audit.why: Sap Magic heals him on attack and its cooldown is reduced every time he casts a spell OR is struck by one — so the more you poke him, the faster the heal comes back. That is a reason to buy Grievous Wounds early rather than as a late luxury.
audit.corrected: Put the mechanic and the timing into breakdown.mid, mid and tradeGood.

edits.before: Maokai has almost no kill pressure on you early — his Sapling Toss (W... E) poke is dodgeable and your Q3 dash lets you out-trade him whenever his Nature's Grasp isn't up.
edits.after: Maokai's threat is the chain, not the poke: Twisted Advance roots on 14s, Bramble Smash knocks you back on 7s, and saplings zone the ground between. Trade only once the root is spent.

edits.before: Maokai brings little kill pressure to lane — his Sapling Toss (E) poke is slow and easy to sidestep, and your Mortal Steel (Q3) dash lets you walk up and out-trade him from level 1. Take the CS you want; just watch his W Twisted Advance root, which is his only real gap-closer and jungle-gank setup. Don't hug the wave into his root range with the enemy jungler nearby.
edits.after: Maokai brings real pressure once Twisted Advance is up — he is untargetable through the dash and roots you on arrival, and Bramble Smash knocks you out of your own Q3 every 7s. Sapling Toss zones the wave from 1100 range. Level 1 is yours before he has the root; after that take safe CS, stay outside 525, and never step up with the jungler unaccounted for.

edits.before: Through levels 3-5 you keep control — every trade where his root and saplings are down is free for you, and your W Spirit Cleave sustains through his poke. At 6 his R Nature's Grasp is a telegraphed root wall you dodge with E Soul Unbound or a simple dash, so you never have to give up priority. Use that priority to shove and roam.
edits.after: Through levels 3-5 he holds the edge — root into knockback into saplings is one combo, and Sap Magic heals back the chip you land, so bring Grievous Wounds. Trade only in the 14s after Twisted Advance is spent. At 6 his R Nature's Grasp is a telegraphed root wall on 130s you can walk out of, so it costs priority, not the lane.

edits.before: After your first item you can shove and dive: your on-hit shreds his passive frame and he has no way to punish the all-in. Late game he settles into a pure utility tank whose Twisted Advance root enables his team — a farmed Yone dodges it and stays relevant, but respect that this is where the tank's scaling and his roams start to bite, so avoid over-extending.
edits.after: After your first item you can shove, but diving a Maokai who heals through Sap Magic is a coin-flip — force it only in the window after Twisted Advance is spent. Late game he settles into a pure utility tank whose root enables his team; a farmed Yone dodges it and stays relevant, but respect the tank's scaling and avoid over-extending into his roams.

edits.before: Dodge Sapling Toss (E) and Q3 dash for free trades
edits.after: Dodge Twisted Advance, then Q3 dash for the trade

notes: This page read as a free lane — 'almost no kill pressure', five of seven rows to Yone — while the data says Yone wins 47.42% of 1280 games, and the packet flags the chart as contradicting the data. I took the mirror's chart, which fits. Bramble Smash was missing from the page entirely despite being a 7s knockback that interrupts your Q3 dash, and spikes[0].text carried a corrupted slot label ('Sapling Toss (W... E)'). The kit's derived grounding flag on Bramble Smash is NOT in Riot's text, so I did not write it — but if it is real it also denies your dash and belongs on the page.
